Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Scrapyard in the browser

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The separate Replay project exports to Godot Web and uses authenticated raw WebRTC data channels for gameplay. Room's WebSocket control connection handles authority leases and rendezvous. The value simulation, asset cache, action admission, checkpoint barrier and migration reducer are shared with native play.

Run the local acceptance gate from the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/web_run.sh

It requires the Godot web export template, Chrome, and the same puppeteer-core installation used by tests/web. Missing prerequisites and failed assertions fail the gate. RSB_LOGS=/absolute/path retains results at a chosen location; otherwise the script prints its temporary directory. RSB_MODES=planned or RSB_MODES=crash selects one scenario. REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 reuses native libraries and the initial WASM build; the export plugin still builds its release module.

The gate starts a local SQLite authority service and three independent Chrome processes. It exercises staging, ability selection, readiness, arena entry, an actual file-input PNG upload, and spray placement. The selected successor's asset consumer pauses deliberately: a checkpoint referencing an unavailable PNG must remain unprepared. After the image arrives and preparation succeeds, the host creates an active zone and a lobbed attack. Handoff or process death then tests exact checkpoint restoration and new combat on the successor.

Before the fault, every peer must be ready in epoch 1 with zero resyncs and zero fragment rejection; each follower must have received exactly one full bootstrap snapshot. After recovery, survivors must retain their seats, display the same 44,459-byte image by SHA-256, and observe continued casts, landings and reactions. At least ten shared authoritative ticks must have identical canonical whole-world hashes. The collector retains at most 1,024 hashes per browser for 20 seconds; it never hashes predicted state as authoritative truth. Screenshots, raw logs, startup counters, hash maps, driver events and summary.json remain available.

Normal browser play now persists its identity, confirmed loadout and upgrades through IndexedDB profiles. Run web_profile_run.sh for the killed- browser reload, conflict and corruption gate. This is separate from full run saves.

web_save_run.sh tests complete solo run saves and persistent sprays: two uploads, active combat, a killed browser, exact resume, continued gameplay, conflicts and invalid-save preservation. F5 waits for a commit receipt. Resume retains the bundled image even if the separately saved preference changed.

The spray picker uses a browser file input, validates the size before copying bytes into Godot, and then runs the ordinary PNG validation/cache/admission path. With persistence enabled it stores the upload after validation and waits for the commit before adopting it. Native environment options have lowercase query equivalents (RSY_NAME becomes name, for example). Coordinated browser play additionally needs coord_url, coord_key, member, incarnation and the provisioned game token. The gate supplies public fixture credentials; it is not an account or credential provisioning service.

Current evidence is local Chrome on arm64 macOS with 120 ms receive delay per participant, direct local ICE and two peers per authority. The driver measures fault-to-continued-combat separately from Room's narrower recovery timer. These are individual scenario measurements, not latency percentiles. Public TLS, STUN/TURN reachability, other browser engines, broader storage/recovery cases, Steam and the full Scrapyard parity matrix remain roadmap work.

The direct browser Room/coordinator path also reads the shared replayIceConfig before opening RTC, using the same validated ICE configuration as the Party path. Invalid configuration rejects the session. This permits relay-only direct test sessions and carries the selected configuration into recovery connections.
